craft_claim: Spare parataxis—short clauses, concrete nouns, few evaluative adjectives—transfers the burden of feeling to the reader and produces unsentimental weight; naming the emotion directly dissipates it.

supporting_evidence.location: The Achievement of Cormac McCarthy, chapters on style and the border novels
supporting_evidence.note: Bell's study treats McCarthy's spare, declarative, image-driven prose and withheld commentary as central to the moral pressure of the work; the reader supplies the judgement the narration refuses.

supporting_evidence.location: Whole novel; desert and atrocity sequences
supporting_evidence.note: The prose records violence as world-fact through concrete noun catalogues and minimal evaluative language; dread and judgement are produced in the reader rather than asserted by the narrator.

supporting_evidence.location: Whole novel; ash landscape and father-son sequences
supporting_evidence.note: Very short declarative sentences and stripped dialogue carry attachment and doom without stating either; tenderness survives because the surface refuses to plead.

counterevidence.note: Section G 'Tonal monotony': unrelieved grimness without contrast habituates and the voice stops signalling, so spare parataxis and concrete catalogues produce weight only while the surface is still doing signalling work; section H item 5 makes contrast, not the catalogue, what restores the register's capacity to mean.

scope: Prose fiction, memoir, and reportage that seeks unsentimental weight.
exceptions: Some traditions (for example high rhetorical lament) deliberately work through elaborate, patterned language; the technique is a choice, not a universal rule.
